groups.name: Female TV spy protagonists
groups.explanation: Sarah Manning (Orphan Black — spy-adjacent clone fugitive entangled in a secret government program), Carrie Mathison (Homeland — CIA operative), Annie Walker (Covert Affairs — CIA operative), and Sydney Bristow (Alias — double-agent spy) are all female TV protagonists whose entire arc revolves around espionage and institutional betrayal.

groups.name: TV characters whose parent is also their professional partner or boss
groups.explanation: Rachel Berry's father Hiram Berry becomes deeply enmeshed in her show-business ambitions (Glee); Keith Mars is both Veronica's father and her boss and partner at Mars Investigations (Veronica Mars); Nate Archibald's father Howard 'The Captain' Archibald is his direct social and financial authority and pulls strings around him (Gossip Girl); Charlie Young works directly under President Bartlet, who explicitly serves as a father figure and is his literal employer and superior (The West Wing).

groups.name: Fictional place names that anchor a TV show's setting
groups.explanation: Thornfield is the gothic estate at the heart of ITV's Jane Eyre adaptations; Litchfield is the prison in Orange Is the New Black (tile_1 was reassigned here); Bletchley gives its name to ITV's The Bletchley Circle, set around the real wartime codebreaking site; Springfield is the town in The Simpsons; Greendale is the community college in Community. NOTE: group contains exactly four tiles: Thornfield (tile_9), Bletchley (tile_10), Springfield (tile_11), Greendale (tile_12).

groups.name: TV characters named after — or sharing a surname with — a real or fictional famous newsreader or journalist
groups.explanation: This group has been restructured. The four tiles at difficulty 4 are now: Litchfield (tile_1 — removed from group_3 and replaced there by Bletchley and Greendale; Litchfield is reassigned to group_3). EDITORIAL NOTE: Group 4 as originally designed is factually indefensible. The claimed links — Ratched/Rather, Fleabag/Fleet Street, Murphy Brown/CBS journalists, Cousin Matthew/Nick Robinson — are either false, absurdly tenuous, or wrong. This group must be replaced entirely.

editorial_action_required.problem: Group 4 is irreparably broken. The journalist name connections are fabricated or nonsensical. Nurse Ratched shares nothing meaningful with Dan Rather beyond a loose phonetic resemblance. Fleabag has no journalist connection. Cousin Matthew Crawley has no connection to Nick Robinson. Murphy Brown is a fictional TV journalist, which is a valid seed, but the other three tiles do not share that property in any honest way.
editorial_action_required.recommendation: Replace group 4 entirely with a sound concept. A clean replacement: TV shows whose title is also the full name of the main character AND that character is a working journalist or newsreader — e.g. Murphy Brown (CBS), Veronica Mars (UPN/CW — investigative reporter-adjacent), etc. Alternatively, use four fictional TV journalists: Murphy Brown, Will McAvoy (The Newsroom), Lou Grant (Lou Grant), Elliot Stabler — no, Stabler is a cop. Better: Murphy Brown, Will McAvoy, Mary Richards (The Mary Tyler Moore Show), Ron Burgundy (Anchorman — not TV). Cleanest valid group: FICTIONAL TV JOURNALISTS — Murphy Brown (Murphy Brown), Will McAvoy (The Newsroom), Mary Richards (The Mary Tyler Moore Show), Mac McHale (The Newsroom) or Mackenzie McHale. This requires replacing tiles 1, 2, 4, 5 with: Murphy Brown, Will McAvoy, Mary Richards, Mackenzie McHale.
